p: Two short lists: questions about this handbook, and the technical notes the pool-violation notice links to. Placeholder text for now.
Who is it for? Everyone serving a church stage production — leadership, cast, crew, and volunteers.
Can we adapt it? Yes. Treat it as a starting point and adjust to your church's calendar and context.
Where does the content come from? The D7460N/EASTER handbook, rendered here through the shared AutoCSS front-end.
Why did a notice appear? The data asked for an element not in the shared component pool, so it was not rendered — the notice surfaces that instead of dropping it silently.

What is the component pool? A curated allow-list of element prototypes (the shared pool.html) the front-end clones. If a tag is neither on the page nor in the pool, nothing is created — a deliberate guard.
How do I add an element to the pool? Add its prototype to the shared pool.html, then reference it from your JSON by its tag name; the injector clones one per array item.
Where do error details go? Here, in this technical list — the pool-violation notice links to this section.
